A common exterior neighbor of a present edge must have a first signature disjoint from both endpoints. Exhaustive accepted side-zero or triangle-cover obstruction therefore proves an edge zero when the accepted spectral state requires an exterior common neighbor.
Iterated support-zero proofs must use already certified zeros or another independently justified dependency scheme; simultaneous circular proposals are not certificates.
